title: EGA projective-bundle projectivity
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. In the EGA/Illusie--Laszlo--Orgogozo convention, $f$ is *projective in the projective-bundle sense* if, for some quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal E$ of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], $X$ is isomorphic over $S$ to a closed subscheme of the projective bundle $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)$, the relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj] of the quasi-coherent symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] with its grading by symmetric degree [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], with $f$ the resulting structure morphism. This is the projective-bundle convention distinguished from the finite-projective-space (H-projective) convention [def-kun-projective].

projective morphism is a closed subscheme of P(E) for a finite type quasi-coherent module
Projective morphism of schemes via closed immersion into projectivization of a quasi-coherent sheaf of finite type
A morphism of schemes is projective if it factors as a closed immersion into the relative Proj of the symmetric algebra of a finite type quasi-coherent module followed by its structure morphism
Projectivization of a quasi-coherent module on a scheme is the relative Proj of its symmetric algebra, and projective means a closed subscheme of such a projectivization
